newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares off to a slow start on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares off to a slow start on Wednesday.

text.p: Singapore shares got off to a slow start on Wednesday with buyers sidelined, dealers said.
"There's no action and no sign of any," said one dealer with a local institution.
"The market really is very flat at the moment," said another.
The Straits Times Industrials Index proved the point, slipping back 7.23 points to 1,969.87 by 0240 GMT
Electronics stocks again were the main focus of early trading activity, but the Stock Exchange of Singapore's electronics index slipped too, losing 2.42 points to 151.56.
Computer maker IPC Corp dominated early activity ahead of interim results expected later in the day.
Five million IPC shares changed hands by 0235 GMT, seeing the stock leap 12 percent, or Singapore $0.055, to S$0.505.
Fellow technology sector counter Creative Technology was an early loser, dropping S$2.00 to S$32.00.
Top early gainer was the Thai Prime investment fund which rose US$0.20 to S$9.50.
